title: structured output: constrained decoding unify backends and fix tokenizer/regex/CFG edgecases
author: Diego Martinez
release_notes: Fixes tokenizer and regex edgecases in constrained decoding backends (CFG + regex), unifies behavior across sampling/beam backends, and improves OpenAI-compat layer mappings. Adds deterministic tests and fuzz harnesses; no API surface breakage.
description: Motivation: Constrained decoders (CFG, regex, tokenizer-based constraints) have diverged behavior across backends (sampling, beam, and streaming) and exposed tokenizer edgecases (surrogate pairs, combining marks, leading/trailing whitespace) that cause structured-output regressions and OpenAI-compat mismatches. This PR unifies the decoding contract across backends, fixes tokenizer normalization bugs, and hardens the OpenAI compatibility layer mapping for regex/grammar constraints. Summary of changes: - Introduced a unified constrained-decoding adapter layer that normalizes constraints into a backend-agnostic intermediate form. - Fixed tokenizer boundary handling for UTF-8 combining characters, zero-width joiners, and stray whitespace tokens that previously allowed invalid token splits inside grammar terminals. - Improved regex constraint compilation to respect tokenizer token boundaries and pure-regex terminal anchors (\A/\z semantics mapped to tokenized sequence anchors). - Added a deterministic streaming path for constrained decoding that preserves constraint invariants during slow token emission and reconnects safely after partial flushes. - Harmonized sampling/backtracking behavior between sampling and beam backends when a constraint requires prefix insertion/rollback. - Extended the OpenAI compatibility shim to accept both legacy "pattern" and new "regex_cfg" forms and normalize them to the intermediate form. - Added extensive unit + integration tests covering CFG grammars, regex constraints, and tokenizer edgecases (including fuzz tests for Unicode boundary cases). - Updated docs and examples in the OpenAI-compat examples folder to highlight tokenizer-sensitive constraints and recommended normalization patterns. Why this matters: Customers using structured output (tool / function calling, JSON outputs) experienced subtle failures where outputs violated grammars or produced malformed tokens in downstream parsers. This PR reduces class of these failures and makes behavior consistent across deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private). Backwards compatibility: Constraint API surface did not change; the OpenAI-compat layer accepts both legacy and new forms. Most customers will not need to change prompts, but complex regex/CFG users may benefit from updated docs. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag `constrained_decoding_v2` for one-week canary on staging then gradual rollout to hosted API. Observability: Added metrics for constraint-failure-rate, tokenizer-boundary-fixes-applied, and streaming-reconnects. Testing: Added deterministic replay tests, cross-backend parity tests, and a new fuzz harness that found several edgecases fixed here. CI: full test suite and new fuzz job included. See commits and files changed for details.
